what: the internal time alignment of the n_TOF detectors, measured in situ on the file being analysed
kind: OFFLINE. A property of the PROCESSING, not of the hardware -- re-measure after any reprocessing or UserInput change

offsets_to_apply.why: on this processing every subsystem is already within a few ns of the others: liquid-vs-wall -0.8..+0.2 ns, wall-vs-plastic per channel RMS 2.3 ns inside a 20 ns logic pulse. Applying a stale offset is as harmful as ignoring a live one -- measure, then decide.

measure_per_file.wall_top_bottom_ns: the per-segment t_top - t_bottom used to pair the two ends of a bar. On v12 it is within +-5.5 ns; on the OFFICIAL processing of the same run it is +-32..39 ns with one -77.5 ns outlier. That structure was the old flash-finder / leading-edge timing, removed by the wall shape fitting of v4_walshapes. Pairing around a 38 ns offset that is no longer there loses most genuine pairs. Use fast_singles.measure_tb_offsets (seconds).

tflash_repair.why: ntof_dream_merge/tflash_repair.py was built for the BROKEN official flash finding. On v12 it is not a no-op: it would shift LIQC/LIQD by ~15 ns and add 25 ns RMS on PSSC, while the stored time base already has the liquids within 1 ns of the walls. ntof_io defaults it ON -- turn it off explicitly.

flash_vs_divert_off_calibration.note: the liquids reproducing the divert-off calibration to 0.1-0.5 ns is two independent measurements confirming each other. The plastics are 31-50 ns away, exactly as flash_timing/README.md warns: take PSS per run.
